text: The moon was up. The sandy earth was cool.
Sunny wandered slow along a winding track.
She heard a scratch, a snuffle, and a shuffle —
something digging in the soft and sandy ground.
A little bilby with the softest ears,
long and silky, twitching at each sound.
Silver-grey, with eyes like drops of night,
and a long dark tail tipped bright as chalk.
“Hello,” said Sunny. “What are you digging for?”
“A cosy burrow, deep and cool,” it said.
Its little paws threw sand in gentle arcs,
digging down to where it's dark and warm.
“The bush gets cold,” the bilby softly spoke.
“But down below it's snug the whole night long.”
They sat a while and watched the quiet stars
come twinkling out above the sleepy bush.
The bilby's ears grew droopy, soft, and low.
“It's time,” it yawned, “to go on down to bed.”
It slipped into its burrow, safe and deep,
and curled up warm beneath the cool dark earth.
Sunny found a hollow, lined with leaves,
and snuggled down beneath a wattle tree.
The bush was still. The moon was soft and low.
Everything was quiet, warm, and safe.
Her eyes grew heavy under drifting stars.
One slow blink… then another… then no more.
And Sunny slept as soundly as the bilby,
deep in dreams beneath the gentle night.
Goodnight, Sunny. Goodnight, little bilby.
Goodnight, sleepy bush. Goodnight, little one.
